# Single-Data Analysis on Observed ACTG175 {#sec-single-data}

:::{.callout-important title="Real-data setting: no ground-truth classification"}
This section analyses the **actual ACTG175 data** -- not a simulated
trial.  The true benefit subgroup in a real trial is **unknown**; it
is the object the analysis is trying to estimate.  We therefore
report the subgroup ForestSearch identifies and the resulting
arm-specific HRs, but we **do not** compute classification metrics
(sens / spec / PPV) against any reference subgroup -- there is no
clinical truth to classify against.  Classification is only
meaningful in the simulation setting of @sec-sims, where the DGM
fixes a known $Q$.
:::

Before any simulation, run ForestSearch on the **actual ACTG175
data** with `details = TRUE` to examine every step of the procedure:
LASSO screening, GRF variable importance, candidate enumeration, and
bootstrap consistency.

::: {.callout-note title="What the analysis methods see"}
The analysis candidate set (passed to `forestsearch()` /
`grf.subg.harm.survival()` as `confounders.name`) is:

- **Continuous** (`r length(analysis_continuous_vars)`):
  `r paste(analysis_continuous_vars, collapse = ", ")`
- **Binary** (`r length(analysis_binary_vars)`):
  `r paste(analysis_binary_vars, collapse = ", ")`

The methods discover cuts on the continuous covariates themselves;
the TRUE cuts (age $>$ `r actg_age_cut`, preanti $\le$
`r actg_preanti_cut`) are **not** provided.
:::

```{r single-data-fs}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "ForestSearch on observed ACTG175 (click to expand)"
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

fs_actg <- tryCatch(
  suppressWarnings(forestsearch(
    df.analysis            = actg_df,
    confounders.name       = confounders_analysis,
    outcome.name           = "time_months",
    event.name             = "cens",
    treat.name             = "treat",          # SWITCHED: ddI = 1
    id.name                = "id",
    hr.threshold           = fs_hr_threshold,
    hr.consistency         = fs_hr_consistency,
    pconsistency.threshold = fs_pconsistency_thresh,
    fs.splits              = fs_splits,
    n.min                  = fs_n_min,
    d0.min                 = fs_d0_min,
    d1.min                 = fs_d1_min,
    maxk                   = fs_maxk,
    by.risk                = fs_by_risk,
    vi.grf.min             = fs_vi_grf_min,
    use_lasso              = FALSE,
    use_grf                = TRUE,
    is.RCT                 = TRUE,
    details                = TRUE,
    quiet                  = FALSE,
    seedit                 = sim_seed,
    parallel_args          = list(
      plan = "sequential", workers = 1, show_message = FALSE
    )
  )),
  error = function(e) {
    warning("ForestSearch on observed data failed: ", e$message)
    NULL
  }
)

timings$single_data_fs <- proc.time()[3] - t0
cat(sprintf("\nForestSearch (real data) completed in %.1f sec\n",
            timings$single_data_fs))
```

## Examine Result

```{r examine-single-data-fs}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Examine FS result on observed ACTG175 (click to expand)"

cat("\n=== ForestSearch Result (Observed ACTG175) ===\n")

if (!is.null(fs_actg) && !is.null(fs_actg$grp.consistency)) {
  sg <- fs_actg$grp.consistency$sg.harm
  if (!is.null(sg) && length(sg) > 0 && !all(is.na(sg))) {
    cat("Subgroup identified:", paste(sg, collapse = " & "), "\n")

    df_est <- fs_actg$df.est
    in_H  <- df_est$treat.recommend == 0
    in_Hc <- df_est$treat.recommend == 1
    cat(sprintf("  Size(H): %d,  Size(Hc): %d\n",
        sum(in_H), sum(in_Hc)))

    if (sum(in_H) >= 10) {
      fit_H <- coxph(Surv(time_months, cens) ~ treat,
                     data = df_est[in_H, ])
      hr_H <- exp(coef(fit_H))
      cat(sprintf("  HR(H, switched):  %.3f  (inverted: %.3f)\n",
          hr_H, 1 / hr_H))
    }
    if (sum(in_Hc) >= 10) {
      fit_Hc <- coxph(Surv(time_months, cens) ~ treat,
                      data = df_est[in_Hc, ])
      hr_Hc <- exp(coef(fit_Hc))
      cat(sprintf("  HR(Hc, switched): %.3f  (inverted: %.3f)\n",
          hr_Hc, 1 / hr_Hc))
    }

    fit_itt <- coxph(Surv(time_months, cens) ~ treat, data = df_est)
    hr_itt <- exp(coef(fit_itt))
    cat(sprintf("  HR(ITT, switched): %.3f  (inverted: %.3f)\n",
        hr_itt, 1 / hr_itt))
  } else {
    cat("No subgroup identified by ForestSearch.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("ForestSearch did not return grp.consistency.\n")
}
```


## GRF Standalone on Observed Data

```{r single-data-grf}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "GRF standalone on observed ACTG175 (click to expand)"

grf_actg <- tryCatch(
  grf.subg.harm.survival(
    data             = actg_df,
    confounders.name = confounders_analysis,
    outcome.name     = "time_months",
    event.name       = "cens",
    treat.name       = "treat",
    id.name          = "id",
    dmin.grf         = grf_dmin,
    frac.tau         = grf_frac_tau,
    maxdepth         = grf_maxdepth,
    RCT              = TRUE,
    sg.criterion     = grf_sg_criterion,
    seedit           = sim_seed,
    details          = TRUE
  ),
  error = function(e) {
    warning("GRF on observed data failed: ", e$message)
    NULL
  }
)

if (!is.null(grf_actg) &&
    !is.null(grf_actg$sg.harm.id) &&
    length(grf_actg$sg.harm.id) > 0L) {
  cat("GRF subgroup:",
      paste(grf_actg$sg.harm.id, collapse = " & "), "\n")
  grf_H <- grf_actg$data$treat.recommend == 0
  cat(sprintf("  Size(H): %d,  Size(Hc): %d\n",
      sum(grf_H), sum(!grf_H)))
} else {
  cat("GRF: no subgroup identified.\n")
}
```


## FS vs GRF Concordance on Observed Data

When a method does not detect a subgroup, its classification is "all
subjects to $Q^c$" (`treat.recommend = 1` for everyone).
`compare_fs_subgroups()` handles this automatically -- no manual
fallback is needed.

```{r single-data-concordance}
#| code-fold: true

if (!is.null(fs_actg) && !is.null(grf_actg)) {
  sg_compare <- compare_fs_subgroups(
    fs1                = fs_actg,
    fs2                = grf_actg,
    label1             = "ForestSearch",
    label2             = "GRF Standalone",
    id.name            = "id",
    subgroup_notation  = "benefit",
    title              = "FS vs GRF: Subgroup Membership Concordance",
    subtitle           = "ACTG175 observed data (survival benefit search, raw continuous)",
    font_size          = 13
  )
  sg_compare$table
}
```


# Creating the ACTG175 DGM {#sec-dgm}

Because `setup_gbsg_dgm()` is specific to the GBSG dataset, we use
`generate_aft_dgm_flex()` directly.  This requires the analyst to
supply the prepared dataset, specify all modelling choices, and
define the subgroup explicitly.

The key function arguments are:

- `data`: the prepared analysis dataset with `y`, `event`,
  `treat`, and all `z*` factor columns.
- `factor_vars`: character vector of **all** binary confounder
  names (here, `z1`--`z12`).  These are used as covariates in
  the AFT model fitted to the observed data.
- `subgroup_vars` / `subgroup_cuts`: define the harm subgroup
  $H$.  `subgroup_cuts` specifies the factor level (here, `1L`)
  that indicates membership.
- `model`: `"alt"` embeds a treatment-by-subgroup interaction;
  `"null"` fits a uniform treatment effect (no HTE).
- `k_inter`: multiplier on the interaction coefficient (AFT
  log-time scale).  Higher values produce larger HR(H).
- `k_treat`: multiplier on the main treatment coefficient.
  Usually `1.0` (retain the observed ITT effect).
- `n_super`: size of the super-population drawn from the fitted
  AFT model.  $5000$ is sufficient for stable HR estimates.


## Step 1: Prepare the Analysis Dataset

The DGM is built on the **switched** treatment data so that the
benefit subgroup $Q$ appears as a "harm" subgroup in the standard
ForestSearch framework.  The `treat` column in `dfa` is already
the switched indicator (ddI = 1, ZDV+ddI = 0).

```{r prepare-actg-dgm}
#| code-fold: false

# Prepare the ACTG175 data for generate_aft_dgm_flex()
# Column names here must match the *_var arguments below.
# Note: 'treat' is already the SWITCHED indicator from the prep step.
dfa        <- actg_df
dfa$y      <- dfa$time_months # outcome in months (days / 30.4375)
dfa$event  <- dfa$cens        # 1 = event, 0 = censored
# 'treat' is the switched indicator (ddI=1, ZDV+ddI=0)

cat("DGM input data:\n")
cat("  N =", nrow(dfa), "\n")
cat("  treat = 1 (ddI monotherapy):", sum(dfa$treat == 1), "\n")
cat("  treat = 0 (ZDV+ddI combination):", sum(dfa$treat == 0), "\n")
cat("  (Treatment is SWITCHED for benefit search)\n")
```


## Step 2: Build the DGM (Alternative Hypothesis)

```{r create-dgm-alt}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

dgm_alt <- generate_aft_dgm_flex(
  data            = dfa,
  outcome_var     = "y",
  event_var       = "event",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  continuous_vars = dgm_continuous_vars,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  model           = "alt",
  k_inter         = dgm_k_inter_init,
  k_treat         = dgm_k_treat,
  n_super         = dgm_n_super,
  seed            = sim_seed,
  verbose         = TRUE
)

# Enrich the DGM with controlled direct effect (CDE) quantities.
# compute_dgm_cde() adds individual-level potential outcomes
# (theta_0, theta_1, loghr_po) to the super-population.  These are
# required by build_estimation_table() and interpret_estimation_table()
# to compute CDE bias and RMSE metrics.  Always call this after
# creating any alternative-hypothesis DGM.
dgm_alt <- compute_dgm_cde(dgm_alt)
dgm_alt <- add_compat_aliases(dgm_alt)

cat("\n=== ACTG175 Alternative DGM ===\n")
cat("  HR(H):",   round(dgm_alt$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup,      3), "\n")
cat("  HR(Hc):",  round(dgm_alt$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup,     3), "\n")
cat("  HR(ITT):", round(dgm_alt$hazard_ratios$overall, 3), "\n")
cat("  AHR(H):",  round(dgm_alt$hazard_ratios$AHR_harm,     3), "\n")
cat("  AHR(Hc):", round(dgm_alt$hazard_ratios$AHR_no_harm,    3), "\n")
cat("  H prevalence:",
    round(100 * mean(dgm_alt$df_super$flag_harm), 1), "%\n")

timings$dgm_alt <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```

### Time-Scale Sanity Check {#sec-timescale-check}

The single most common simulation failure is building the DGM on one
time scale (e.g., months) and then passing `analysis_time` in a different
scale.  This results in a follow-up window far shorter
or longer than the DGM event-time distribution, producing either
universal censoring or no censoring at all.

The diagnostic below verifies that the DGM's implied median event time
(`exp(mu)`) is in the same ballpark as the observed data and that
`analysis_time` is on the correct scale.

```{r timescale-check}
#| code-fold: false

# ── KM-based median (handles censoring correctly) ────────────────
# The naive median(dfa$y[dfa$event == 1]) is biased downward because
# subjects with longer true event times are disproportionately
# censored and never enter the event == 1 subset.  The Kaplan-Meier
# estimator accounts for censoring and returns NA when the median is
# not reached within follow-up.
sf_obs <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(y, event) ~ 1, data = dfa)
km_summary       <- summary(sf_obs)$table
observed_median  <- km_summary[["median"]]
dgm_median       <- exp(dgm_alt$model_params$mu)

if (is.na(observed_median)) {
  # Median not reached within follow-up — common when censoring is
  # heavy.  Fall back to the 25th-percentile event time, which is
  # almost always estimable, and report it as a less-stringent
  # sanity check.
  km_quantiles    <- quantile(sf_obs, probs = 0.25)$quantile
  observed_q25    <- km_quantiles[["25"]]
  cat(sprintf(
    "Observed median event time (KM):  not reached within follow-up\n"))
  cat(sprintf(
    "Observed 25th percentile (KM):    %.1f months\n", observed_q25))
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
    "Observed median event time (KM):  %.1f months\n", observed_median))
}
cat(sprintf("DGM implied median (exp(mu)):     %.1f months\n", dgm_median))
cat(sprintf("analysis_time:                    %.0f months\n", sim_analysis_time))

if (sim_analysis_time < dgm_median * 0.5) {
  warning("analysis_time is much shorter than DGM median -- ",
          "expect heavy administrative censoring!")
}
if (sim_analysis_time > dgm_median * 10) {
  warning("analysis_time is much longer than DGM median -- ",
          "nearly all events will be observed (minimal censoring).")
}
```


## Step 3: Calibrate for Target HR {#sec-calibrate}

### Why calibrate?

The DGM's `k_inter` parameter controls the strength of the
treatment-by-subgroup interaction on the AFT (log-time) scale.
Because the mapping from `k_inter` to the Cox-model hazard ratio
HR(H) is non-linear and depends on the specific covariate
distribution, censoring structure, and baseline hazard, we cannot
set `k_inter` analytically to achieve a desired HR(H).  Instead,
we search over a grid of candidate values and select the one that
yields an HR(H) closest to the target.

A target HR(H) of `r cal_target_hr` is used here because it
represents a clinically meaningful level of harm --- treatment
doubles the hazard in the subgroup --- and matches the simulation
scenarios in León et al. (2024).  Users should choose their target
based on the effect size they want their simulation to be powered
to detect.

**Note:** `calibrate_k_inter()` automates this process for GBSG-based
DGMs.  For non-GBSG datasets, the manual grid search shown here is
required.  This is a known limitation and will be addressed in a
future release.

```{r calibrate-k-inter}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

cal_results <- data.frame(
  k_inter = cal_k_grid,
  hr_H    = NA_real_,
  hr_Hc   = NA_real_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (i in seq_along(cal_k_grid)) {
  dgm_k <- tryCatch(
    generate_aft_dgm_flex(
      data            = dfa,
      outcome_var     = "y",
      event_var       = "event",
      treatment_var   = "treat",
      continuous_vars = dgm_continuous_vars,
      factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
      subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
      subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
      model           = "alt",
      k_inter         = cal_k_grid[i],
      k_treat         = dgm_k_treat,
      n_super         = dgm_n_super,
      seed            = sim_seed,
      verbose         = FALSE
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (!is.null(dgm_k)) {
    cal_results$hr_H[i]  <- dgm_k$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup
    cal_results$hr_Hc[i] <- dgm_k$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup
  }
}

# Find k_inter closest to target
cal_valid  <- cal_results[!is.na(cal_results$hr_H), ]
best_idx   <- which.min(abs(cal_valid$hr_H - cal_target_hr))
k_inter_best <- cal_valid$k_inter[best_idx]

cat(sprintf(
  "Calibration: k_inter = %.2f gives HR(H) = %.3f (target: %.1f)\n",
  k_inter_best, cal_valid$hr_H[best_idx], cal_target_hr
))

timings$calibrate <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```


```{r calibration-plot, fig.height=5}
#| fig-cap: "Calibration of k_inter: HR(H) as a function of the interaction parameter."

ggplot(cal_valid, aes(x = k_inter)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = hr_H,  colour = "HR(H)"),  linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = hr_Hc, colour = "HR(Hc)"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cal_target_hr, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.0, linetype = "dotted",
             colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(
    data = cal_valid[best_idx, ],
    aes(x = k_inter, y = hr_H),
    colour = "red", size = 4, shape = 16
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("HR(H)" = "firebrick", "HR(Hc)" = "steelblue")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "k_inter",
    y = "Hazard Ratio",
    title = "ACTG175 DGM Calibration",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Best: k_inter = %.2f -> HR(H) = %.3f (target: %.1f)",
      k_inter_best, cal_valid$hr_H[best_idx], cal_target_hr
    ),
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```


## Step 4: Create Calibrated DGM

```{r dgm-calibrated}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

dgm_calibrated <- generate_aft_dgm_flex(
  data            = dfa,
  outcome_var     = "y",
  event_var       = "event",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  continuous_vars = dgm_continuous_vars,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  model           = "alt",
  k_inter         = k_inter_best,
  k_treat         = dgm_k_treat,
  n_super         = dgm_n_super,
  seed            = sim_seed,
  verbose         = TRUE
)
# Enrich with CDE potential outcomes (required for estimation tables)
dgm_calibrated <- compute_dgm_cde(dgm_calibrated)
dgm_calibrated <- add_compat_aliases(dgm_calibrated)

cat("\n=== Calibrated ACTG175 DGM ===\n")
cat("  HR(H):",   round(dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup,      3), "\n")
cat("  HR(Hc):",  round(dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup,     3), "\n")
cat("  HR(ITT):", round(dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$overall, 3), "\n")

timings$dgm_calibrated <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```


## Step 5: Create Null DGM {#sec-dgm-null}

Under `model = "null"`, the treatment effect is **homogeneous**
across all patients --- no treatment effect heterogeneity.
Treatment is still beneficial for everyone; there is simply no
subgroup with a different treatment effect.  Any subgroup
detected under the null is a false positive.

By default, `k_treat = 1` preserves the fitted ITT treatment
effect.  For the benefit-search / switched-treatment setup here,
the fitted switched-scale ITT HR is the reciprocal of the
original beneficial HR.  If the original HR = 0.84, the switched
HR = 1/0.84 = 1.19.  This sits below the threshold (c1 =
`r fs_hr_threshold`) but the gap is narrower than in
harm-search scenarios.  The default behaviour (preserved fitted
ITT effect) is the conservative, realistic choice; the
$L_\text{eff}$ calibration procedure accounts for this when
selecting thresholds.

::: {.callout-note title="Optional: widen the gap from c1 with `null_target_hr`"}
If you want to study type-I-error inflation **in isolation** of
the proximity to c1, you can target a specific switched-scale
ITT HR for the null DGM by setting `null_target_hr` in the setup
chunk.  The code below solves for the `k_treat` value that
produces the requested target.

The solver is approximate: `k_treat` multiplies the AFT log-time
treatment coefficient, but the realised Cox HR also depends on
the censoring distribution and the covariate distribution, so
the constructed HR will be close to but not exactly equal to
`null_target_hr`.  After construction we re-check the realised
ITT HR; if it is materially off, iterate.

This is **not** a different research question -- the topic
remains differential treatment effects across subgroups.  It is
simply a way to widen the gap between the marginal ITT HR and
c1 so that the FPR you measure is driven by search-space
multiplicity rather than by the marginal signal sitting close to
the detection threshold.

Setting `null_target_hr = NULL` (the default) preserves the
fitted ITT effect (`k_treat = 1`).
:::

```{r dgm-null}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

# ── Solve for k_treat under the optional null_target_hr ──────────
# The default keeps k_treat = dgm_k_treat (typically 1.0, preserving
# the fitted ITT effect).  When null_target_hr is non-NULL, we solve:
#   k_treat_null = log(target_hr_switched) / log(fitted_hr_switched)
# fitted_hr_switched comes from the alt DGM's overall hazard ratio,
# which is on the switched scale by construction in this vignette.
dgm_k_treat_null <- dgm_k_treat
if (!is.null(null_target_hr)) {
  fitted_log_hr <- log(dgm_alt$hazard_ratios$overall)
  if (abs(fitted_log_hr) < 1e-8) {
    stop("Fitted ITT log-HR is ~0; cannot rescale to a target HR. ",
         "Leave null_target_hr = NULL.")
  }
  dgm_k_treat_null <- log(null_target_hr) / fitted_log_hr
  message(sprintf(
    "null_target_hr = %.3f  -->  k_treat (null) = %.3f  (fitted log-HR = %.3f)",
    null_target_hr, dgm_k_treat_null, fitted_log_hr))
}

dgm_null <- generate_aft_dgm_flex(
  data            = dfa,
  outcome_var     = "y",
  event_var       = "event",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  continuous_vars = dgm_continuous_vars,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  model           = "null",
  k_treat         = dgm_k_treat_null,
  n_super         = dgm_n_super,
  seed            = sim_seed,
  verbose         = TRUE
)
dgm_null <- add_compat_aliases(dgm_null)

cat("\n=== ACTG175 Null DGM ===\n")
cat("  k_treat used:           ", round(dgm_k_treat_null, 3), "\n")
if (!is.null(null_target_hr)) {
  cat("  null_target_hr (target):", round(null_target_hr, 3), "\n")
}
cat("  HR(ITT, switched):      ", round(dgm_null$hazard_ratios$overall, 3), "\n")
cat("  HR(ITT, original):      ", round(1 / dgm_null$hazard_ratios$overall, 3), "\n")
cat("  c1 threshold:           ", fs_hr_threshold, "\n")
cat(sprintf("  Gap (c1 - HR_switched):  %.3f\n",
            fs_hr_threshold - dgm_null$hazard_ratios$overall))

timings$dgm_null <- proc.time()[3] - t0
```

### Illustrative `k_treat` values: HR(ITT) and gap to c1

To give the reader a concrete sense of how `k_treat` controls the
marginal ITT effect and therefore the gap from c1, the table below
constructs three illustrative null DGMs at `k_treat` $\in \{0.5,
1.0, 1.5\}$ using the same data, factor lists, super-population
size, and seed as the main `dgm_null` above.  The default
(`k_treat = 1.0`) preserves the fitted ITT effect; **larger**
`k_treat` amplifies the marginal benefit, pushing the
switched-scale HR further above 1 and *narrowing* the gap to c1;
**smaller** `k_treat` attenuates the marginal effect toward
HR $\approx 1$ and *widens* the gap.

```{r dgm-null-illustrate}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Build three illustrative null DGMs and tabulate (click to expand)"

# Three illustrative null DGMs.  These are NOT used in the simulation
# loop below; the simulation uses `dgm_null` from the previous chunk
# (constructed with k_treat = dgm_k_treat_null).  The grid here is
# purely a didactic table so the reader can see how k_treat moves
# HR(ITT) and the gap to c1.
k_treat_grid <- c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5)

illust_rows <- lapply(k_treat_grid, function(k) {
  d <- generate_aft_dgm_flex(
    data            = dfa,
    outcome_var     = "y",
    event_var       = "event",
    treatment_var   = "treat",
    continuous_vars = dgm_continuous_vars,
    factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
    subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
    subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
    model           = "null",
    k_treat         = k,
    n_super         = dgm_n_super,
    seed            = sim_seed,
    verbose         = FALSE
  )
  d <- add_compat_aliases(d)
  hr_switched <- as.numeric(d$hazard_ratios$overall)
  data.frame(
    k_treat     = k,
    hr_switched = hr_switched,
    hr_original = 1 / hr_switched,
    gap_to_c1   = fs_hr_threshold - hr_switched
  )
})
illust_tbl <- do.call(rbind, illust_rows)

gt::gt(illust_tbl) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title    = "Illustrative null DGMs: HR(ITT) and gap to c1 by k_treat",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "ACTG175 benefit search, switched scale; c1 = %.3f, n_super = %d",
      fs_hr_threshold, dgm_n_super
    )
  ) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    k_treat     = "k_treat",
    hr_switched = "HR(ITT, switched)",
    hr_original = "HR(ITT, original)",
    gap_to_c1   = gt::md("Gap (c1 \u2212 HR_switched)")
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns  = c(hr_switched, hr_original, gap_to_c1),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = k_treat, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style    = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(rows = k_treat == 1.0)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_footnote(
    footnote = paste0(
      "k_treat = 1.0 (bold row) preserves the fitted ITT effect; this is ",
      "the default null DGM. Smaller k_treat attenuates the marginal ",
      "effect toward HR \u2248 1 (widening the gap to c1); larger k_treat ",
      "amplifies the effect (narrowing the gap). The realised HR is ",
      "approximate -- the AFT log-time scaling does not map exactly to ",
      "the Cox HR, which also depends on the censoring and covariate ",
      "distributions."
    )
  )
```


# Single Trial Simulation {#sec-single-trial}

Before running the full simulation study, we generate a single
simulated trial to verify that the pipeline produces sensible data.
This is a useful sanity check: the simulated event rate, subgroup
prevalence, and ITT HR should be broadly consistent with the DGM
parameters.

```{r simulate-single}
sim_data <- simulate_from_dgm(
  dgm           = dgm_calibrated,
  n             = single_n,
  rand_ratio    = single_rand_ratio,
  seed          = single_seed,
  analysis_time = sim_analysis_time,
  cens_adjust   = sim_cens_adjust
)

cat("Simulated ACTG175 trial:\n")
cat("  N =", nrow(sim_data), "\n")
cat("  Events =", sum(sim_data$event_sim),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(sim_data$event_sim)))
cat("  Harm subgroup size =", sum(sim_data$flag_harm),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(sim_data$flag_harm)))

fit_sim <- coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim, data = sim_data)
cat("  Estimated ITT HR =", round(exp(coef(fit_sim)), 3), "\n")
```

## Censoring Diagnostic {#sec-cens-check}

The `check_censoring_dgm()` function compares the simulated censoring
distribution against the observed data used to build the DGM.  Large
discrepancies suggest a time-scale mismatch or a poorly calibrated
censoring model.

```{r censoring-diagnostic}
check_censoring_dgm(
  sim_data = sim_data,
  dgm      = dgm_calibrated
)
```


## Baseline Characteristics (Simulated Trial) {#sec-single-demog}

```{r single-demographics}
# Label treatment arms for the table
sim_data$treat_label <- factor(
  sim_data$treat_sim,
  levels = c(0, 1),
  labels = c("Combo (ZDV+ddI)", "ddI monotherapy")
)

# Simulated data has z1-z12 as factor columns from the DGM super-population.
# Identify which z-variables are present
z_vars <- grep("^z[0-9]+$", names(sim_data), value = TRUE)
z_vars_present <- z_vars[z_vars %in% names(sim_data)]

create_summary_table(
  data       = sim_data,
  treat_var  = "treat_label",
  vars_continuous  = "y_sim",
  vars_categorical = z_vars_present,
  var_labels = c(y_sim = "Follow-up time (months)"),
  table_title = "Simulated Trial: Baseline Characteristics by Treatment Arm",
  table_subtitle = sprintf("N = %d, Events = %d (%.1f%%)",
    nrow(sim_data), sum(sim_data$event_sim),
    100 * mean(sim_data$event_sim)),
  font_size = 11
)
```


## Kaplan-Meier Analysis (Simulated Trial) {#sec-single-km}

```{r single-km}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.5

dfcount_sim <- weightedsurv::df_counting(
  df        = sim_data,
  by.risk   = fs_by_risk,
  tte.name  = "y_sim",

)

weightedsurv::plot_weighted_km(

```

```{r single-cox-summary}
fit_sim_adj <- coxph(
  Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim + z1 + z2 + z3,
  data = sim_data
)

cat("=== Single Simulated Trial: Cox PH Summary ===\n")
cat(sprintf("  Unadjusted HR: %.3f\n", exp(coef(coxph(
  Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim, data = sim_data)))))
cat(sprintf("  Adjusted HR:   %.3f (z1 + z2 + z3)\n",
    exp(coef(fit_sim_adj)["treat_sim"])))
```


## ForestSearch on Simulated Trial {#sec-single-fs}

::: {.callout-warning title="Single-replicate caveat: realistic-analysis variance"}
Because the analysis methods see covariates in their RAW form (not
the discretised z-factors), variable-screening steps such as LASSO
and GRF must rediscover the truth-defining variables from scratch in
each replicate.  Under modest sample sizes (n = `r sim_n_sample` per
trial here), it is **expected** that any single replicate may fail
to retain the true subgroup-defining variables -- this is the price
of the realistic-analysis pattern, not a bug.

Reliable inference about the method's behaviour comes from the
**full simulation loop** in @sec-results, where the operating
characteristics aggregate across `r nsims_alt` simulations.  The H1
detection rate, classification metrics, and bias diagnostics in
@sec-oc-alt are the appropriate basis for evaluating the method;
the single-replicate output below is a pipeline-sanity check, not a
performance claim.
:::

```{r single-fs}
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

fs_single <- tryCatch(
  suppressWarnings(forestsearch(
    df.analysis            = sim_data,
    confounders.name       = confounders_analysis,
    outcome.name           = "y_sim",
    event.name             = "event_sim",
    treat.name             = "treat_sim",
    id.name                = "id",
    hr.threshold           = fs_hr_threshold,
    hr.consistency         = fs_hr_consistency,
    pconsistency.threshold = fs_pconsistency_thresh,
    fs.splits              = fs_splits,
    n.min                  = fs_n_min,
    d0.min                 = fs_d0_min,
    d1.min                 = fs_d1_min,
    maxk                   = fs_maxk,
    by.risk                = fs_by_risk,
    vi.grf.min             = fs_vi_grf_min,
    use_lasso              = TRUE,
    use_grf                = TRUE,
    is.RCT                 = TRUE,
    details                = TRUE,
    quiet                  = FALSE,
    seedit                 = sim_seed,
    parallel_args          = list(
      plan = "sequential", workers = 1, show_message = FALSE
    )
  )),
  error = function(e) {
    warning("ForestSearch failed: ", e$message)
    NULL
  }
)

timings$single_fs <- proc.time()[3] - t0
cat(sprintf("\nForestSearch completed in %.1f sec\n", timings$single_fs))
```

```{r single-fs-results}
fs_single_detected <- !is.null(fs_single) &&
  !is.null(fs_single$grp.consistency) &&
  !is.null(fs_single$grp.consistency$sg.harm.id) &&
  length(fs_single$grp.consistency$sg.harm.id) > 0

if (fs_single_detected) {
  sg_id <- fs_single$grp.consistency$sg.harm.id
  cat("=== ForestSearch Result (Single Simulated Trial) ===\n")
  cat("  Subgroup:", paste(sg_id, collapse = " & "), "\n")

  df_est <- fs_single$df.est
  in_H   <- df_est$treat.recommend == 0
  true_Q <- sim_data$flag_harm == 1

  tp <- sum(in_H & true_Q); fp <- sum(in_H & !true_Q)
  fn <- sum(!in_H & true_Q); tn <- sum(!in_H & !true_Q)
  cat(sprintf("  n(H) = %d (%.1f%%), n(Hc) = %d\n",
      sum(in_H), 100 * mean(in_H), sum(!in_H)))
  cat(sprintf("  Sensitivity: %.3f\n", tp / max(tp + fn, 1)))
  cat(sprintf("  Specificity: %.3f\n", tn / max(tn + fp, 1)))
  cat(sprintf("  PPV:         %.3f\n", tp / max(tp + fp, 1)))
} else {
  cat("ForestSearch did not identify a subgroup in this single trial.\n")
  cat("This can happen with moderate effect sizes at n =", single_n, "\n")
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
The subgroup identified in this single trial may differ from the true
$Q$ defined by the DGM. The simulation study below evaluates how often
ForestSearch correctly recovers the true subgroup across many replicates.
:::


# Running Simulation Studies {#sec-sims}

## Setup

```{r sim-setup}
#| code-fold: false

plan(multisession, workers = n_workers)
cat("Using", n_workers, "parallel workers\n")

# ── Candidate variable set ────────────────────────────────────
# confounders_base tells run_simulation_analysis() which columns in
# the simulated data to pass to ForestSearch and GRF as candidate
# subgroup-defining variables.  Mirrors the binary vignette: a real
# analyst would NOT know which variables define Q nor where to cut
# them, so the candidate set is the RAW continuous columns
# (age, preanti, wtkg, karnof, cd40, cd80) plus the truly-binary
# factor columns (hemo, homo, drugs, race, gender, symptom).  The
# discretised z1-z12 columns remain on the simulated data frame
# only for the DGM (via factor_vars) and the truth flag --- they
# are NOT candidates for the analysis search.
confounders_actg <- confounders_analysis

# ── ForestSearch parameters ───────────────────────────────────
# These are passed to run_simulation_analysis() and forwarded to
# forestsearch().  The annotations below explain each parameter
# and when you might change it for your own study.
fs_params <- list(
  # Column name mappings — must match simulate_from_dgm() output
  outcome.name           = "y_sim",
  event.name             = "event_sim",
  treat.name             = "treat_sim",
  id.name                = "id",

  # Variable screening flags
  use_lasso              = TRUE,    # LASSO pre-screening (recommended)
  use_grf                = TRUE,    # GRF pre-screening (recommended)

  # Subgroup detection thresholds (see Leon et al. 2024, Section 3)
  # c1: a candidate subgroup must have HR > hr.threshold to be flagged.
  # Increase for more conservative detection; decrease for more power.
  hr.threshold           = fs_hr_threshold,
  # c2: in each bootstrap replicate, the subgroup HR must exceed this
  # value.  Typically set to 1.0 (any harm signal).
  hr.consistency         = fs_hr_consistency,
  # The proportion of bootstrap replicates in which the subgroup HR
  # exceeds c2.  The paper default is 0.90.
  pconsistency.threshold = fs_pconsistency_thresh,

  # Computational and sample-size constraints
  fs.splits              = fs_splits,    # Bootstrap replicates (400 is default)
  n.min                  = fs_n_min,     # Minimum subgroup size (both arms)
  d0.min                 = fs_d0_min,    # Minimum events, control arm
  d1.min                 = fs_d1_min,    # Minimum events, treatment arm
  maxk                   = fs_maxk,      # Max subgroup-defining variables
  by.risk                = fs_by_risk,   # Risk-table granularity (time units)
  vi.grf.min             = fs_vi_grf_min, # GRF variable importance threshold
  seedit                 = sim_seed,      # Reproducible split-half consistency

  # Two-stage estimation: after identifying a subgroup, re-estimates
  # the treatment effect using an independent hold-out sample.
  # Recommended for bias correction.
  use_twostage           = TRUE,
  twostage_args          = list(),

  # GRF tuning (applies to ForestSearch's internal GRF pre-screening)
  tune_grf               = grf_tune,

  # Inner parallelism: ForestSearch runs sequentially within each
  # worker.  The outer loop (foreach) parallelises across replicates.
  parallel_args          = list(
    plan = "sequential", workers = 1, show_message = FALSE
  )
)

# -- GRF standalone parameter overrides ----------------------------------------
grf_params <- list(
  dmin.grf     = grf_dmin,
  frac.tau     = grf_frac_tau,
  maxdepth     = grf_maxdepth,
  sg.criterion = grf_sg_criterion,
  tune_grf     = grf_tune
)

# ── Simulation configuration ─────────────────────────────────
sim_config <- list(
  n_sample      = sim_n_sample,
  analysis_time = sim_analysis_time,
  cens_adjust   = sim_cens_adjust
)
```


## Alternative Hypothesis Simulations

```{r run-alt}
cat("Running", nsims_alt, "simulations under H1...\n")
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

results_alt_raw <- foreach(
  sim = seq_len(nsims_alt),
  .errorhandling = "pass",
  .options.future = list(
    packages = c("forestsearch", "survival", "data.table", "future"),
    seed = TRUE
  )
) %dofuture% {
  # Reset plan inside workers to prevent nested parallelism.
  # Each worker runs ForestSearch sequentially; the outer foreach
  # loop parallelises across simulation replicates.
  future::plan("sequential")
  run_simulation_analysis(
    sim_id           = sim,
    dgm              = dgm_calibrated,
    n_sample         = sim_config$n_sample,
    analysis_time    = sim_config$analysis_time,
    cens_adjust      = sim_config$cens_adjust,
    confounders_base = confounders_actg,
    cox_formula_adj  = cox_formula_adj,
    n_add_noise      = sim_n_noise,
    run_fs           = run_fs,
    run_fs_grf       = run_fs_grf,
    run_grf          = run_grf,
    fs_params        = fs_params,
    grf_params       = grf_params,
    verbose          = FALSE
  )
}

timings$sims_alt <- proc.time()[3] - t0
results_alt <- forestsearch::collect_results(results_alt_raw, "H1 alt")

cat("Completed in", round(timings$sims_alt / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
if (n_failed_alt > 0) cat(sprintf("  *** %d FAILED ***\n", n_failed_alt))
cat("Results:", nrow(results_alt), "rows\n")
```

# Results {#sec-results}

## Metrics Glossary {#sec-glossary}

The operating-characteristics tables below report three groups of
metrics:

- **detection**: the proportion of simulations where ForestSearch
  (or GRF) identifies *any* subgroup ($\texttt{any.H} = 1$).
  Under the alternative, this is detection power; under the null,
  it is the false-positive rate (type I error).

- **classification**: among simulations where a subgroup was
  detected, how well the identified subgroup $\hat{H}$ overlaps
  with the true subgroup $H$.  Includes sensitivity (proportion
  of true $H$ members captured), specificity (proportion of
  $H^c$ members correctly excluded), and positive predictive value
  (PPV, proportion of $\hat{H}$ that truly belongs to $H$).

- **cde_estimates**: bias and root-mean-square error (RMSE) of
  the controlled direct effect (CDE) estimator for the treatment
  effect within $\hat{H}$ and $\hat{H}^c$, relative to the true
  DGM values.  The CDE is defined at the individual level via
  potential outcomes and represents the causal estimand
  (see León et al. 2024, Section 2.2).


## Operating Characteristics Under H1 {#sec-oc-alt}

The simulation engine runs on the **switched** treatment scale.
When `subgroup_notation = "benefit"` is passed to the table
functions, they automatically invert all hazard ratios to the
**original** scale (HR < 1 = benefit from ZDV+ddI) and apply
Q/Qc notation.

::: {.callout-note title="Trimming Cox-HR plug-in columns for the estimation tables"}
The plug-in Cox HR estimates (`hr.H.hat`, `hr.Hc.hat`) can blow up
in single replicates where the identified subgroup -- typically
$Q^c$ -- has zero events in one arm.  When that happens the Cox
coefficient is unbounded and the realised HR is effectively
$0$ or $\infty$ on the switched scale, which after inversion to
the benefit scale produces extreme display values that swamp the
table's `Avg`, `SD`, and `Max` columns even when the AHR-based
columns (`ahr.H.hat`, `ahr.Hc.hat`) and bias-corrected columns
(`hr.H.bc`, `hr.Hc.bc`) remain well-behaved.

Because the package's existing trimming infrastructure
(`SGplot_estimates(trim_fraction = ...)`) is plumbed only into
the violin plotter and not into `build_estimation_table()`, we
apply a symmetric quantile-based winsorization to the four Cox-HR
columns at the vignette level **on the switched scale**, before
passing the results to the table functions.  AHR columns are
left untouched.

Set `trim_fraction <- NULL` below to disable; the table will then
show raw (untrimmed) statistics.  The default of `0.01` clamps
the bottom and top 1% of values per column.
:::

```{r oc-alt-trim-setup}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Trimming helper (click to expand)"

# Symmetric quantile winsorization of Cox-HR plug-in columns.
# Operates on the SWITCHED scale (the columns as stored in
# `results_alt` / `results_null` -- inversion to the benefit scale
# happens inside build_estimation_table()).
#
# Returns a copy of `results` with trimmed values and a "trim_log"
# attribute summarising n_trimmed per column.
winsorize_hr_columns <- function(results,
                                 trim_fraction = 0.01,
                                 cols = c("hr.H.hat", "hr.Hc.hat",
                                          "hr.H.bc",  "hr.Hc.bc")) {
  if (is.null(trim_fraction) || trim_fraction <= 0) {
    return(results)
  }
  if (trim_fraction >= 0.5) {
    stop("trim_fraction must be < 0.5")
  }
  out <- as.data.frame(results)
  trim_log <- data.frame(column = character(0), n_trimmed = integer(0),
                         lower = numeric(0), upper = numeric(0),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (col in intersect(cols, names(out))) {
    v <- out[[col]]
    finite_idx <- is.finite(v)
    if (sum(finite_idx) < 5L) next
    lo <- stats::quantile(v[finite_idx], trim_fraction,    na.rm = TRUE)
    hi <- stats::quantile(v[finite_idx], 1 - trim_fraction, na.rm = TRUE)
    flag <- finite_idx & (v < lo | v > hi)
    out[[col]][flag & v < lo] <- lo
    out[[col]][flag & v > hi] <- hi
    trim_log <- rbind(trim_log, data.frame(
      column     = col,
      n_trimmed  = sum(flag, na.rm = TRUE),
      lower      = as.numeric(lo),
      upper      = as.numeric(hi),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }
  attr(out, "trim_log") <- trim_log
  out
}

# Apply to both result sets.  The trimmed versions are passed to
# build_estimation_table() below; format_oc_results() uses the
# untrimmed versions because it summarises detection / classification
# (not effect-size summaries).
trim_fraction        <- 0.01      # 1% symmetric; set NULL to disable
results_alt_trimmed  <- winsorize_hr_columns(results_alt,  trim_fraction)
results_null_trimmed <- winsorize_hr_columns(results_null, trim_fraction)

cat("=== Cox-HR winsorization summary (switched scale) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("  trim_fraction = %s\n",
            if (is.null(trim_fraction)) "NULL (disabled)"
            else sprintf("%.3f", trim_fraction)))
cat("  H1 (alt) trimmed columns:\n")
if (!is.null(attr(results_alt_trimmed, "trim_log")))
  print(attr(results_alt_trimmed, "trim_log"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("  H0 (null) trimmed columns:\n")
if (!is.null(attr(results_null_trimmed, "trim_log")))
  print(attr(results_null_trimmed, "trim_log"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Distribution of Identified Subgroups

The distribution of the identified subgroup $\hat H$ under H1
(calibrated HTE) and H0 (null) is rendered by
`forestsearch::plot_sg_distribution()`.  Under the benefit search,
the expected H1 anchor is the DGM's
$Q = \{\texttt{z1} = 1\} \cap \{\texttt{z2} = 1\}$ (age > `r actg_age_cut`
and preanti $\le$ `r actg_preanti_cut`).  Charts adapt their height to
the number of bars via `sgdist_fig_height()` and auto-halve the
percentage threshold (up to twice) when no label clears the initial
value.

```{r oc-sgdist-build}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Build subgroup-distribution plots (click to expand)"

plot_sgdist_alt <- plot_sg_distribution(
  results              = results_alt[results_alt$analysis == "FS", ],
  any_col              = "any.H",
  label_col            = "sg.def",
  min_pct              = sgdist_min_pct_alt,
  top_k                = sgdist_top_k,
  show_other           = sgdist_show_other_alt,
  max_halvings         = 2L,
  bar_label_inside     = TRUE,
  placeholder_on_empty = TRUE,
  title                = "HTE: Subgroups Identified (H-hat)",
  wrap_width           = 30
)

plot_sgdist_null <- plot_sg_distribution(
  results              = results_null[results_null$analysis == "FS", ],
  any_col              = "any.H",
  label_col            = "sg.def",
  min_pct              = sgdist_min_pct_null,
  top_k                = sgdist_top_k,
  show_other           = sgdist_show_other_null,
  max_halvings         = 2L,
  bar_label_inside     = TRUE,
  placeholder_on_empty = TRUE,
  title                = "Null: Subgroups Identified (H-hat)",
  wrap_width           = 30
)

h_alt  <- sgdist_fig_height(attr(plot_sgdist_alt,  "n_bars"))
```

```{r oc-null-hrdist, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
)
```


# Theoretical Detection Probability {#sec-detection}

The detection probability is the theoretical power of ForestSearch's
bootstrap consistency rule to flag a subgroup with a given HR, given
the expected subgroup size and censoring proportion.  This curve
provides a reference for interpreting the empirical detection rate
observed in the simulation.

The `method = "cubature"` argument uses numerical integration
(via the `cubature` package) to compute the joint probability
that the subgroup HR exceeds `hr.threshold` (c1) and that the
proportion of bootstrap replicates exceeding `hr.consistency`
(c2) is at least `pconsistency.threshold`.  An alternative
`method = "normal"` uses a normal approximation.

```{r detection-curve, fig.height=6}
n_sg_expected <- sim_config$n_sample *
  mean(dgm_calibrated$df_super$flag_harm)
prop_cens <- mean(results_alt$p.cens)

cat("Expected subgroup size:", round(n_sg_expected), "\n")
cat("Censoring proportion:",   round(prop_cens, 3), "\n")
cat("True HR(H):",             round(dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, 3), "\n")

prob_detect <- compute_detection_probability(
  theta          = dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup,
  n_sg           = round(n_sg_expected),
  prop_cens      = prop_cens,
  hr_threshold   = fs_params$hr.threshold,
  hr_consistency = fs_params$hr.consistency,
  method         = "cubature"
)

cat("\nTheoretical P(detect):", round(prob_detect, 3), "\n")
cat("Empirical FS:",
    round(mean(results_alt[
      results_alt$analysis == "FS", "any.H"
    ]), 3), "\n")

# Generate curve
detection_curve <- generate_detection_curve(
  theta_range       = det_theta_range,
  n_points          = det_n_points,
  n_sg              = round(n_sg_expected),
  prop_cens         = prop_cens,
  hr_threshold      = fs_params$hr.threshold,
  hr_consistency    = fs_params$hr.consistency,
  include_reference = TRUE,
  verbose           = FALSE
)

plot_detection_curve(
  detection_curve,
  add_reference_lines = TRUE,
  add_threshold_line  = TRUE,
  title = sprintf(
    "Detection Curve (n_sg=%d, cens=%.0f%%, c1=%.2f)",
    round(n_sg_expected), 100 * prop_cens,
    fs_params$hr.threshold
  )
)

abline(v = dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, lty = 2, col = "blue")
```


# Timing Summary {#sec-timing}

```{r timing-summary}
timings$total <- (proc.time() - t_vignette_start)["elapsed"]

timing_df <- data.frame(
  Stage = c(
    "DGM creation (H1)",
    "k_inter calibration",
    "DGM calibrated",
    "DGM creation (H0)",
    "Single-trial ForestSearch",
    "Simulations H1",
    "Simulations H0",
    "Summarize H1",
    "Summarize H0",
    "Total"
  ),
  Seconds = c(
    timings$dgm_alt,
    timings$calibrate,
    timings$dgm_calibrated,
    timings$dgm_null,
    timings$single_fs,
    timings$sims_alt,
    timings$sims_null,
    timings$summarize_alt,
    timings$summarize_null,
    timings$total
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
timing_df$Minutes <- timing_df$Seconds / 60
timing_df$Hours   <- timing_df$Seconds / 3600

gt::gt(timing_df) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title    = "Computational Timing Summary",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "%d H1 + %d H0 sims | %d workers",
      nsims_alt, nsims_null, n_workers
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = Seconds, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = Minutes, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = Hours,   decimals = 3) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    Stage   = "Stage",
    Seconds = "Time (sec)",
    Minutes = "Time (min)",
    Hours   = "Time (hr)"
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(rows = Stage == "Total")
  )
```

### Projection for Production Runs

```{r projection}
# Per-replicate cost by stage
time_per_alt  <- timings$sims_alt / nsims_alt
time_per_null <- timings$sims_null / nsims_null

proj_alt   <- time_per_alt * prod_alt
proj_null  <- time_per_null * prod_null
proj_other <- timings$total - timings$sims_alt - timings$sims_null
proj_total <- proj_alt + proj_null + proj_other

proj_df <- data.frame(
  Component = c("H1 simulations", "H0 simulations", "Other (DGM, calibration, summaries)",
                "Total"),
  Count     = c(
    sprintf("%d replicates", prod_alt),
    sprintf("%d replicates", prod_null),
    "---",
    sprintf("%d + %d", prod_alt, prod_null)
  ),
  `Per replicate` = c(
    sprintf("%.1f sec", time_per_alt),
    sprintf("%.1f sec", time_per_null),
    "---",
    "---"
  ),
  Projected = c(
    sprintf("%.1f min", proj_alt / 60),
    sprintf("%.1f min", proj_null / 60),
    sprintf("%.1f min", proj_other / 60),
    sprintf("%.1f min (%.1f hours)", proj_total / 60, proj_total / 3600)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

gt::gt(proj_df) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title = sprintf("Projected Time: %d alt + %d null", prod_alt, prod_null),
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Based on current run (%d + %d on %d workers)",
      nsims_alt, nsims_null, n_workers
    )
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(rows = Component == "Total")
  )
```


# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## Key Differences from the GBSG Simulation

The ACTG175 dataset introduces several features that test
ForestSearch under different conditions than the GBSG template:

1. **Larger sample size** ($N \approx 1{,}000$ vs $686$): more
   candidate subgroups survive the `n.min` filter, potentially
   increasing $L_{\text{eff}}$ and the procedure-level FPR.

2. **More confounders** ($12$ vs $7$): the combinatorial search
   space is larger, testing GRF and LASSO screening effectiveness.

3. **Different event rate**: ACTG175 has a lower event rate than
   GBSG, which reduces $d_{\text{eff}}$ per subgroup and may
   affect detection power.

4. **Different subgroup structure**: the age $\times$ preanti subgroup
   is defined by continuous variables discretised at clinically
   motivated cutpoints, rather than the GBSG's receptor-status
   $\times$ menopausal-status interaction.

5. **Time scale**: ACTG175 times have been converted from days to months for
   AFT model parametrisation but not the HR-scale operating
   characteristics.

## Reloading Saved Results

When `save_results = TRUE`, the simulation bundle is saved as an
`.rds` file in the `_data/` directory.  To reload for downstream
analysis:

```r
bundle <- readRDS("_data/actg175_survival_benefit_simulations_50alts_50nulls.rds")

# Core results (data.tables)
results_alt  <- bundle$results_alt
results_null <- bundle$results_null

# DGM objects (class "aft_dgm_flex")
dgm_cal  <- bundle$dgm_calibrated
dgm_null <- bundle$dgm_null

# True effects
bundle$true_effects$hr_Q     # HR(Q) on switched scale
bundle$true_effects$ahr_Q    # AHR(Q)
bundle$true_effects$k_inter  # calibrated interaction multiplier

# Reproduce tables
format_oc_results(results_alt, subgroup_notation = "benefit", ...)
build_estimation_table(results_alt, dgm = dgm_cal,
                       subgroup_notation = "benefit", ...)
```


## Limitations

- The ACTG175 benefit subgroup definition (age $> `r actg_age_cut`$
  AND preanti $\leq `r actg_preanti_cut`$) is based on the
  exploratory analysis in León et al. (2024, §4.2). The true
  treatment effect heterogeneity pattern in ACTG175 is unknown.

- The benefit-search approach (treatment switching) adds a layer
  of indirection: all DGM, simulation, and ForestSearch operations
  use the switched treatment indicator, and results must be
  inverted for interpretation on the original treatment scale.

- `generate_aft_dgm_flex()` requires more analyst judgment than
  `setup_gbsg_dgm()`. The variable discretisation, subgroup
  definition, and censoring calibration must all be specified
  manually.

- The simulation count (`r nsims_alt` sims) is for demonstration.
  Production studies should use $\geq 500$ simulations for stable
  operating characteristics (Monte Carlo SE for a 50% rate $\approx
  2.2\%$ at 500 sims).

- The adjusted Cox formula (`cox_formula_adj`) includes only 3 of
  12 confounders.  This is a deliberate choice for parsimony, but
  users should select confounders appropriate for their study
  design.

- `calibrate_k_inter()` does not yet support non-GBSG datasets;
  the manual grid search in @sec-calibrate is the current
  workaround.
